empirical_typing_authority.fact_used: Frozen V1.1 accepts verified derived Boolean DAG roots as GUARDED_ITE guards/children without adding a new rule form.

objects.standard_circuit_model: Acyclic bounded-fanin Boolean circuits over {AND, OR, NOT} with free input variables and fanout by sharing.
objects.size_measure_V1_1: Number of distinct hash-consed DAG nodes plus total literal/support occurrences stored by AFFINE_XOR nodes.
objects.size_measure_standard: Number of Boolean gates plus input-wire/literal occurrences needed to encode the circuit.

lemma.name: POLYNOMIAL_REPRESENTATION_EQUIVALENCE_OF_V1_1_BOOLEAN_DAGS_AND_STANDARD_BOOLEAN_CIRCUITS
lemma.statement: For every Boolean function represented by a standard bounded-fanin Boolean circuit C there is a V1.1 Boolean DAG P computing the same function with size O(|C|). Conversely, every V1.1 Boolean DAG P has an equivalent standard Boolean circuit C_P whose size is O(N_ITE_CONST + SUM_AFFINE_SUPPORT), hence polynomial in the frozen V1.1 representation size.
lemma.scope: Boolean-function representation only. This does not include the cost of discovering P from a source relation, producing Pi_domain, proving Skolem validity, or translating arbitrary proof derivations between proof systems.

forward_translation_standard_to_V1_1.input_x: AFFINE_XOR(0,{x}) or an already-licensed input/root reference
forward_translation_standard_to_V1_1.sharing: Translate each source circuit gate once and preserve fanout by DAG references/hash-consing.
forward_translation_standard_to_V1_1.bound: O(s) V1.1 nodes for a standard circuit with s gates, apart from representation of already-given inputs.

reverse_translation_V1_1_to_standard.GUARDED_ITE_g_t_f: (g AND t) OR ((NOT g) AND f), constant bounded-fanin overhead.
reverse_translation_V1_1_to_standard.AFFINE_XOR_c_support_t: Balanced or sequential XOR tree on t support bits plus optional negation/constant; O(t) bounded-fanin Boolean gates. XOR itself has constant-size {AND,OR,NOT} implementation.
reverse_translation_V1_1_to_standard.EXISTING_DAG_NODE: Wire/reference only; no semantic gate expansion.
reverse_translation_V1_1_to_standard.sharing: Translate each distinct V1.1 DAG node once.

proof_sketch: The forward direction follows gate-by-gate from the explicit ITE identities for NOT, AND and OR and preservation of DAG sharing.
The reverse direction follows by replacing each ITE by a constant-size bounded-fanin Boolean subcircuit and each t-ary affine XOR by an O(t)-size XOR network.
Both translations preserve the Boolean function exactly by structural induction on DAG/circuit topological order.

consequences.representation_lower_bound_warning: An unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for unrestricted V1.1 witness-DAG representation of an explicit Boolean function, under the stated size measure, would imply a corresponding superpolynomial lower bound for general Boolean circuits for that function.
not_implied: V1.1 can synthesize every small circuit in polynomial time from an arbitrary source formula
V1.1 has polynomial-size proofs/certificates for every relation with small Skolem circuits
V1.1 is polynomially equivalent to SynQBF as a proof system

synqbf_comparison_contract.primary_reference: Akshay et al., Proof Systems for QBF Synthesis: Extracting Skolem and Herbrand Functions, SAT 2026, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.SAT.2026.3
published_facts: Skolem/Herbrand extraction and intermediate game-value computation are polynomial-time in proof size.
The paper states optimality among proof systems that permit efficient Skolem/Herbrand extraction.
The paper gives conditional lower bounds and comparisons/orthogonality with existing QBF proof systems.
A compilation algorithm from arbitrary QBF to SynQBF proofs is provided; this does not by itself imply polynomial compilation for every input family.
next_theory_questions: Define a semantics-preserving map from a restricted SynQBF proof fragment into (Pi_domain, Pi_witness, local V1.1 derivation) and bound proof-size/extraction overhead.
Define a map from frozen V1.1 proof-carrying objects into SynQBF when the source relation is encoded as a QBF with matching dependency discipline.
Separate representation overhead from proof-generation overhead and from extraction overhead.
Do not compare runtimes on arbitrary n before a translation/model-match theorem identifies a meaningful common object.

qbf_strategy_extraction_context.published_context: QBF literature already uses strategy-extraction complexity to transfer restricted circuit hardness into proof-size lower bounds, and shows that some powerful systems such as refutational QRAT cannot have polynomial-time strategy extraction unless P=PSPACE.
qbf_strategy_extraction_context.janus_use: Use these results as proof-system/extraction comparators, not as unrestricted V1.1 DAG lower bounds.

governance_effect.allow_only_if: A future target comes with a lower bound that provably applies to the exact V1.1 representation/proof model, or the research question concerns synthesis/proof/extraction overhead rather than raw circuit existence.
